selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main quality of creation is emphasized at the start of the passage about plants and animals?
questions.answer: Their creation is presented as happening very quickly while still being perfectly ordered.

questions.question: In this section, what does “The Third Truth” focus on most directly?
questions.answer: It focuses on the way living things are created with speed, order, ease, skill, and value.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the manner in which creation happens?
questions.answer: It says creation happens with ease while still showing high skill.

questions.question: According to the passage, who alone can create in this way?
questions.answer: The only one who can do this is the One whose power has no limitation or hardship.

questions.question: How does the passage use comparison as a method of teaching?
questions.answer: It places large and small examples side by side to show they are equally easy for Divine power.

questions.question: Since those problems do not appear, what does the passage conclude?
questions.answer: It concludes that only a unique and all-powerful Being can be behind such creation.

questions.question: How does the passage compare reviving the whole earth with reviving a tree?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: What idea is taught by comparing a mountain-like tree to a tiny seed?
questions.answer: Great outward size and tiny beginnings are both under the same power.

questions.question: Why is the phrase about seeing these deeds important for comprehension?
questions.answer: It reminds readers that the evidence is present in the created world around them.

questions.question: What is the central claim of the passage about how living things are created?
questions.answer: Living things are created swiftly, abundantly, and with perfect order and excellence.

questions.question: Why would combining speed with careful order be meaningful in this argument?
questions.answer: Because quick action usually risks mistakes, but here speed does not lessen precision.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the relation between quantity and quality?
questions.answer: Even when things are very numerous, their quality and uniqueness remain.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from speed, abundance, order, and value appearing together?
questions.answer: Such creation can come only from a single unmatched Creator.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the Creator’s power from this absence of deficiency?
questions.answer: The Creator’s power must be fully capable and unrestricted.

questions.question: What comparison answers the idea that creating a whole group must be harder than creating one individual?
questions.answer: The passage says a whole species is as easy as one of its members.

questions.question: What does the example of the earth and the tree teach?
questions.answer: Reviving something vast and reviving something limited are the same in ease for Him.

questions.question: What is the effect of saying stars and atoms are alike in ease for Him?
questions.answer: It removes the idea that greater size means greater difficulty.

questions.question: If you had to give this passage a short theme, what would it be?
questions.answer: Allah’s power creates all things with equal ease, no matter how great or small.

questions.question: What verse theme introduces this section of the passage?
questions.answer: It begins with a verse about benefits taken from date palms and grapevines as a sign for people who use reason.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the pattern or arrangement of creation?
questions.answer: It says creation is perfectly organized.

questions.question: What difficulty does the passage say is absent even though created things are many and mixed together?
questions.answer: There is no confusion and no flaw.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about power if nothing is difficult for it?
questions.answer: It implies a power that is unlimited and not restricted like created beings are.

questions.question: What result would we expect if such creation were not under perfect control?
questions.answer: We would expect disorder, mistakes, or lack of distinction.

questions.question: What comparison is made between a whole species and one individual?
questions.answer: Bringing an entire kind into existence is said to be as easy as creating one member of it.
